title: Factorial divisibility criterion for divided powers in a torsion-free ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring whose additive group is torsion-free, meaning that $ma=0$ for a positive integer $m$ implies $a=0$. Let $J\subseteq A$ be an ideal generated by a family $(u_s)_{s\in S}$. Suppose that for every $s\in S$ and every integer $n\geq1$ there is $v_{n,s}\in J$ with $u_s^n=n!v_{n,s}$. Then $J$ has a unique ordinary divided-power structure $\theta$ [def-sfb-ordinary-divided-power-structure]. For every $x\in J$ and $n\geq1$, its value $\theta_n(x)$ is the unique element of $J$ satisfying $n!\theta_n(x)=x^n$; in particular $\theta_n(u_s)=v_{n,s}$.

source.place: Tag 07GM (lemma-silly), parts (1)-(4), especially the generator criterion (4).

proof.text: For $z\in J$ put $P(z):\ \forall n\geq1,\ \exists w_n\in J,\ z^n=n!w_n$. We have $P(0)$, and $P(au_s)$ with witnesses $a^nv_{n,s}$. If $P(x)$ and $P(y)$ have witnesses $b_i,c_i$, set $b_0=c_0=1$. The binomial expansion [lem-pur-commutative-ring-binomial-expansion] and $\binom ni i!(n-i)!=n!$ give $(x+y)^n=n!\sum_{i=0}^n b_i c_{n-i}$. For $n>0$ every summand has a positive-index factor in $J$, hence the displayed sum lies in $J$. Every element of the ideal generated by the $u_s$ is a finite sum of multiples $au_s$; induction on the number of summands, starting with zero and applying this addition calculation, proves $P(z)$ for every $z\in J$.

source.place: Tag 07GM (lemma-silly), proof (4), binomial addition and induction on the length of a generator expression.

proof.text: If $n!b=n!c$, then $n!(b-c)=0$; since $n!>0$, torsion-freeness gives $b=c$. Thus the witnesses just constructed define maps $\theta_n:J\to J$ for $n\geq1$ independently of every generator expression, with $n!\theta_n(x)=x^n$. Put $\theta_0(x)=1$. In particular $\theta_1(x)=x$.

Put $B=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, the tensor product of the commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebras $A$ and $\mathbf Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]: a commutative ring with multiplication $(a\otimes q)(b\otimes r)=ab\otimes qr$, unit $1\otimes1$, and ring homomorphisms $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $q\mapsto1\otimes q$, the latter being its rational scalar map. The canonical ring map $f(a)=a\otimes1$ is injective by [lem-trf-torsionfree-rationalization-injective], applied to the additive group of $A$. Let $K=J\cdot B$ be the ideal of $B$ generated by $f(J)$, and apply [lem-sfb-rational-ideal-divided-powers] to $K$, calling its structure $\delta$. Applying $f$ to the defining factorial equation and multiplying by the rational scalar $1/n!$ gives $f(\theta_n(x))=\delta_n(f(x))$ for $x\in J$, $n>0$; for $n=0$ the same equality follows from $f(1)=1$.

source.place: Tag 07GM (lemma-silly), proof (3): embed in the rational algebra and compare with x^n/n!.

proof.text: Check the five axioms of [def-sfb-ordinary-divided-power-structure] by applying the injective map $f$ and using the preceding equality. The images of the two sides of the scalar, sum, and product axioms are respectively $\delta_n(f(a)f(x))=f(a)^n\delta_n(f(x))$, $\delta_n(f(x)+f(y))=\sum_i\delta_i(f(x))\delta_{n-i}(f(y))$, and $\delta_n(f(x))\delta_m(f(x))=\binom{n+m}{n}\delta_{n+m}(f(x))$. They are equal by the corresponding axioms of the rational structure. Since $\theta_m(x)\in J$ for $m>0$, the images in the iteration axiom are $\delta_n(\delta_m(f(x)))=\frac{(nm)!}{n!(m!)^n}\delta_{nm}(f(x))$, again equal. Ring maps preserve these integer coefficients. The first axiom was checked in step 2. Injectivity therefore proves all the required equalities in $A$, so $\theta$ is an ordinary divided-power structure.

source.place: Tag 07GM (lemma-silly), proof (3), verification of the five identities after the injective rational embedding.

proof.text: For any other ordinary divided-power structure $\eta$, its product axiom with indices $1,n-1$ gives $n\eta_n(x)=x\eta_{n-1}(x)$ for $n\geq2$. Induction starting from $\eta_1(x)=x$ yields $n!\eta_n(x)=x^n$ for every $n>0$. The cancellation in step 2 forces $\eta_n(x)=\theta_n(x)$. This proves uniqueness of the structure and uniqueness of every factorial quotient in $J$; the given $v_{n,s}$ is such a quotient at $u_s$, hence $\theta_n(u_s)=v_{n,s}$.

source.place: Tag 07GM (lemma-silly), proofs (1)-(2), factorial identity by induction and uniqueness.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unique_of_factorial_divisibility_on_generators (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (hT : ∀ (m : ℕ) (a : A), 0 < m → m • a = 0 → a = 0) (J : Ideal A) (S : Type v) (u : S → A) (hgen : Ideal.span (Set.range u) = J) (hdiv : ∀ (s : S) (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∃ w ∈ J, u s ^ n = (n.factorial : A) * w) : ∃ θ : DividedPowers J, (∀ η : DividedPowers J, η = θ) ∧ (∀ (x : A), x ∈ J → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → (n.factorial : A) * θ.dpow n x = x ^ n ∧ ∀ (y : A), y ∈ J → (n.factorial : A) * y = x ^ n → y = θ.dpow n x) ∧ (∀ (s : S) (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (w : A), w ∈ J → u s ^ n = (n.factorial : A) * w → θ.dpow n (u s) = w)
